title: ‘Batman: Caped Crusader’ Season 2 Is a Masterful Sequel About the Heroes We Need Now
summary: By paying tribute to wayward working stiffs, the animated series from executive producers J.J. Abrams, Matt Reeves, and Bruce Timm grounds our hero in an evolving compassion that's as apt for young audiences as it is for those of us painfully aware of current events.

title: ‘Butcher, Baker, Nightmare Maker’ Is the Deranged Cult Slasher Every Horror Fan Should Have on Tap
summary: Released in 1981, William Asher's delirious exploitation flick will instantly up your repertory game.

title: For Rising Stars, Good Taste Comes at a Cost — Superhero Films Are Just One Way to Satiate It
summary: While a segment of cinephiles mourn the "loss" of prestigious actors to MCU films, the other options of making blank-check money are arguably even more capitalistic.

title: How a Tiny Pez Dispenser Became TV’s Most Important Story Breadcrumb on ‘Silo’
summary: Rebecca Ferguson, Graham Yost, and director Aric Avelino dish out the candy dispenser facts behind the Apple TV series.

title: Emily Wilson vs. Christopher Nolan, and Why Literary Translators Don’t Make the Best Film Critics
summary: On this week's "Screen Talk," we review Emily Wilson's "review" and discuss "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" and A24's "Tony."

title: IndieWire Names Brent Lang Editor-in-Chief, as Longtime Leader Dana Harris-Bridson Departs
summary: Harris-Bridson will exit in early August, with Lang, the current Executive Editor of Variety, stepping into the role later that month.

title: ‘Nightborn’ Review: Rupert Grint and Seidi Haarla Raise a Bloodthirsty Baby in a Shudder Movie About the Horrors of Motherhood
summary: Hanna Bergholm’s follow-up to "Hatching" wants you to know that having kids is not for the faint of heart.

title: Gregg Araki Made His Reputation Directing Sex in the Age Before Intimacy Coordinators — Did Using One Change His Process?
summary: Araki talks about working with Olivia Wilde, Cooper Hoffman, and intimacy coordinator Yehuda Duenyas to craft the sex scenes in "I Want Your Sex."

title: Becoming Mike Mills: Inside the Two Decades and Unexpected Path Leading to ‘Beginners’
summary: Mills tells IndieWire about his Criterion box set, his Roy Andersson-inspired next film, and how balancing his conceptual art studies and humanist sensibilities was key to his directing breakthrough.

title: Nick Antosca Made ‘Cape Fear’ His Own with Scorsese and Spielberg’s Blessing — and Their Notes
summary: The showrunner of Apple's hit series tells the Filmmaker Toolkit podcast about working with Martin Scorsese and Steven Spielberg as producers, finding a worthy Max Cady in Javier Bardem, and why the finale deviated from the ending of Scorsese's 1991 film.

title: ‘Time Warp’ Review: Young and Queer ‘Rocky Horror’ Fans Stage a Small-Town Drag Production Worthy of Christopher Guest
summary: Outfest: Allison Berg's charming, earnest Wyoming-centered doc follows a "Rocky Horror" troupe as they mount a production against the headwinds of city council censorship efforts.

title: ‘Wild Inside’ Review: Flaco the Owl Can Still Change Your Life (and Maybe the World)
summary: Penny Lane's loving, tender, and fearlessly questioning documentary about the celebrity owl is a film this writer can only take entirely personally. Everyone else can (and should) feel that way, too.
